action: If you received a notice, enrol in the free credit monitoring offered where your Social Security number was involved, and check insurance statements for services you did not receive.
exec: Two separate intrusions at one specialist provider in 2026 mean repeated notification and monitoring costs; the article says it is unclear whether they are related.
plain: A Minnesota epilepsy clinic was hacked for the second time this year, exposing personal and medical details of about 82,500 people.
summary: The Level 4 epilepsy centre detected unauthorised network access on August 10, confirmed on September 17 that personal and health information was compromised, and began mailing notices on October 16 according to HIPAA Journal (October 14 according to Paubox). HHS lists the incident as affecting 82,574 people; an earlier intrusion from March 16 to April 10 affected 80,061. Exposed data may include Social Security numbers, treatment and insurance information. No attacker is named.
title: Minnesota Epilepsy Group reports second cyberattack of 2026, affecting 82,574 people

validation.note: Two publishers state the core facts: HIPAA Journal and Paubox (read 22 Nov; it cites the HHS breach portal for 82,574 and 80,061 and confirms 10 August and 17 September). They differ on when notices began: 16 October (HIPAA Journal) vs 14 October (Paubox). The Massachusetts notice answered 403; MEG's own notice was not read.

review.note: Dates, 82,574 and 80,061 figures, data types match HIPAA Journal; exec's incomplete remediation was unsupported (article says unclear if related), reworded

evidence.quote: According to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the incident impacted 82,574 individuals.
The breach was reported to the HHS as having impacted 80,061 individuals.
